title: API gateway admission control middleware (per-tenant/per-route) + circuit breaker hooks
creator: Ethan Park
project: Reliability Program: Hosted circuit breakers + load shedding
content:
## Goal
Add an admission-control middleware to the Hosted API gateway to reject/degrade requests early (before routing/runtime) when the platform is saturated or a circuit breaker is open.

This middleware is the first line of defense for overload protection. It must be:
- tenant-aware (per-tenant overrides + tier defaults)
- route/model-aware (chat vs embeddings vs rerank; plus model selectors)
- consistent with customer-facing overload semantics (ADR-014)
- layered correctly with routing/runtime backpressure signals (ADR-015)

## Why this exists
During bursts, we currently let too much work into the system, which cascades into:
- p99 tail-latency blowups (queue amplification + streaming concurrency)
- elevated timeouts/5xx from downstream timeouts rather than explicit overload
- noisy-neighbor effects between tenants and between routes/models

Early rejection with stable semantics is preferable to letting requests time out.

## Scope
### In scope
1) Gateway admission middleware in request path for Hosted API:
- token bucket rate limiting per tenant per route (RPS)
- concurrency caps per tenant per route (in-flight)
- optional request cost weighting (prompt-length / expected tokens) behind a feature flag (phase 2)

2) Hooks for breaker state + policy engine:
- consult policy engine for effective limits (tier defaults + tenant overrides)
- consult breaker state provider (regional + per-route/model where applicable)
- emit breaker/admission decisions to metrics + traces

3) Correct error response + headers:
- map to ADR-014 overload error codes and JSON payload
- include correlation/request IDs
- set Retry-After consistently when rejecting due to overload

### Out of scope (this ticket)
- Smart Routing fallback decisions (ENG-4824)
- runtime queue/decode saturation export details (ENG-4825)
- SLO classification rules updates (handled in SLO toolkit)

## Requirements / acceptance criteria
- [ ] Per-tenant/per-route token bucket enforced in gateway (default tier policy + override)
- [ ] Per-tenant/per-route concurrency cap enforced in gateway (default tier policy + override)
- [ ] If breaker is OPEN (or policy says "shed"), gateway returns overload response immediately with stable semantics (ADR-014)
- [ ] Error response includes:
  - HTTP status (429 for tenant limit exceeded; 503 for platform overload/breaker open)
  - `error.code` from ADR-014 (e.g., `OVERLOAD_GATEWAY_ADMISSION`, `RATE_LIMIT_TENANT`, `CONCURRENCY_LIMIT_TENANT`)
  - `error.message` (customer-safe)
  - `request_id` / `correlation_id`
  - `retry_after_ms` field and `Retry-After` header when applicable
- [ ] Metrics emitted with bounded cardinality; no tenant_id labels on high-volume counters (see Metrics section)
- [ ] Middleware can be dark-launched (observe-only) + canaried by region and tenant allowlist
- [ ] Integration tests cover: allow, reject-429, reject-503, header correctness, Retry-After presence, and idempotency behavior for retries

## Proposed design
### Placement
API Gateway (edge) request handler pipeline:
1. AuthN/AuthZ + tenant identification (existing)
2. Usage enforcement hooks (existing; called before admission decision for certain plans)
3. Admission Control middleware (new)
4. Routing selection (existing)
5. Upstream call to runtime/router

Rationale: keep bad traffic out early; do not depend on runtime health to reject; avoid feedback loops per ADR-015.

### Decision inputs
- Tenant:
  - tenant_id
  - tier (self-serve / enterprise hosted / dedicated hosted)
- Route:
  - /v1/chat/completions
  - /v1/embeddings
  - /v1/rerank
  - streaming vs non-streaming
- Optional selectors (phase 2 / behind flag):
  - model family (normalized) to avoid per-model cardinality blowups

### Policy evaluation
Policy engine returns an effective policy document for (tenant, route, region):
- `rps_limit` (token bucket)
- `concurrency_limit`
- `retry_after_seconds` default for shed
- `mode`: enforce | observe | disabled
- `breaker_binding`: what breaker keys to consult (regional, route-level)

Implementation note: gateway should cache policy lookups for short TTL (e.g., 5–15s) and respect explicit cache-bust on policy updates.

### Rate limiter implementation
- Token bucket keyed by (tenant, route)
- Backed by shared in-memory limiter on each gateway instance; initial rollout is per-instance (no cross-instance global fairness)
  - We accept approximate behavior initially; goal is protecting downstream, not strict billing-grade rate enforcement.
- Spillover guidance:
  - If over limit: 429 + `RATE_LIMIT_TENANT`
  - Include `Retry-After` based on bucket refill estimate (min/max clamped)

### Concurrency limiter implementation
- Semaphore keyed by (tenant, route)
- In-flight counter is released when upstream response completes (including streaming completion)
- Streaming nuance:
  - For streaming endpoints, concurrency is often the limiting factor. We should apply stricter defaults (tier-based) vs non-streaming.
  - Ensure cancellation propagates and releases semaphore promptly.

### Breaker state hook
- Breaker state provider interface in gateway:
  - `GetBreakerState(key) -> {CLOSED, OPEN, HALF_OPEN}`
- Keying:
  - `hosted:{region}` (minimum)
  - optionally `hosted:{region}:{route}` if routing/runtime exports support it (coordinate with ENG-4825)
- Behavior:
  - OPEN => reject early with 503 + `OVERLOAD_GATEWAY_ADMISSION` + Retry-After (policy default)
  - HALF_OPEN => allow limited sample (phase 2; can treat as CLOSED for initial rollout)

## Error semantics (ADR-014 alignment)
- 429 (tenant-scoped):
  - code: `RATE_LIMIT_TENANT` or `CONCURRENCY_LIMIT_TENANT`
  - message: "Request rate/concurrency limit exceeded for your account. Retry with backoff."
  - Retry-After required
- 503 (platform overload):
  - code: `OVERLOAD_GATEWAY_ADMISSION`
  - message: "Service temporarily overloaded. Retry with backoff."
  - Retry-After required

All overload responses must include `request_id` and an opaque `correlation_id` suitable for Support.

## Metrics / telemetry
### Must have
- `gateway_admission_decisions_total{decision="allow|reject", reason="rate_limit|concurrency|breaker_open|policy_shed", route=..., region=...}`
- `gateway_admission_inflight{route=..., region=...}` (gauge)
- `gateway_admission_retry_after_seconds_bucket` (histogram; no tenant label)
- `gateway_admission_policy_fetch_total{result="hit|miss|error"}`

### Explicit anti-requirements
- Do NOT label high-volume metrics with `tenant_id`.
- Do NOT label by raw model name.

### Debuggability
- Structured logs on reject path (sampled): include tenant_id, route, reason, effective limits, request_id/correlation_id.
- Traces: add span tag `admission.decision` and `admission.reason`.

## Rollout plan
1) Observe-only (dark launch):
- compute decision, emit metrics/logs, but do not reject
- validate false positive rate and policy correctness

2) Canary enforcement:
- enable enforcement for one region (us-east) + small tenant allowlist
- monitor: shed rate, 5xx/timeouts, p95/p99 latency, retry storms

3) Progressive enablement:
- expand allowlist to tier defaults for self-serve first (more tolerant), then enterprise hosted
- dedicated hosted should default to higher caps and preferential admission; verify with Product (Lauren) and SRE (Rafael)

4) GA:
- enable across regions; finalize dashboard + runbook references

## Test plan
- Unit tests for limiter behavior (token bucket math, concurrency release on cancellation)
- Integration tests (gateway harness):
  - 429 with Retry-After
  - 503 with Retry-After
  - correlation_id propagation
  - streaming cancellation releases concurrency slot
- Load test (perf-canary): burst scenario with mixed prompt lengths to validate improved timeouts vs explicit rejects

## Open questions
- Do we want separate concurrency limits for streaming vs non-streaming on same route? (Recommendation: yes; use route variant key `chat_streaming`.)
- Should HALF_OPEN be supported at gateway in v1, or treat as CLOSED? (Recommendation: treat as CLOSED initially; rely on routing/runtime for probing.)
- Global fairness: per-instance limiter can be gamed by horizontal client spread; acceptable for first release but note for follow-up.

## Links
- ADR-014: Hosted overload error taxonomy (status mapping + payload)
- ADR-015: Admission control layering (gateway vs routing vs runtime)
- ENG-4822: Define overload error codes and payloads
- ENG-4825: Export runtime saturation signals
- PR (WIP): redwood monorepo PR-18433 (gateway admission control middleware)

## Follow-ups (not blocking GA unless called out)
- Add request-cost weighting (estimated tokens) to reduce long-prompt blast radius
- Add HALF_OPEN sampling at gateway if we need faster recovery gating
- Explore shared distributed rate limiter for stricter per-tenant guarantees
comments: 2025-10-08 (Ethan Park): Created. This is the gateway-side admission layer described in ADR-015. Please keep metrics cardinality constraints front-and-center; SRE will page us if we blow up Prometheus.

2025-10-10 (Rafael Mendes): P0 from SRE perspective. For initial enforcement, I’d rather we under-shed (observe-only first) than accidentally block a big tenant. Also: Retry-After must be consistent to avoid retry storms.

2025-10-14 (Benji Okafor): Policy engine can return route-scoped defaults + tenant overrides. We’ll need a short TTL cache in gateway; please avoid per-request RPC. I’ll post the draft schema changes in ENG-4821 thread.
2025-10-18 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Make sure tenant identity is resolved before limiter keys. We’ve had issues where some routes don’t attach tenant_id until after auth middleware—double-check ordering.

2025-10-22 (Amara Diallo): Implemented token bucket + concurrency semaphore keyed by (tenant, route_variant). Added observe-only mode behind `GATEWAY_ADMISSION_MODE=observe`. Still need to wire breaker provider and finalize error mapping to ADR-014 payload struct.
2025-10-28 (Christine Wong): Please ensure streaming disconnects release concurrency slots. We saw leaked inflight counters during earlier streaming experiments; add a test that cancels mid-stream.

2025-11-05 (Amara Diallo): Breaker hook wired using `breaker_state_client` (regional key only for now). If OPEN, returns 503 with `OVERLOAD_GATEWAY_ADMISSION`. Added Retry-After (clamped 1s–30s) from policy default. Needs review on exact header value format (seconds) vs ms field.

2025-11-12 (Aisha Bello): Metrics proposal looks good. Please add a separate counter for policy fetch errors; we want an alert if the policy engine is down and the gateway defaults to fail-open vs fail-closed.

2025-11-18 (Ethan Park): PR-18433 opened. Requesting reviews from SRE + Policy Engine. Note: we intentionally kept limiter in-process per instance for v1; documented follow-up for distributed fairness.

2025-11-21 (Rafael Mendes): Reviewed PR. Blocking items: (1) Retry-After missing on 429 concurrency rejects in one codepath, (2) ensure `correlation_id` is always present (even when upstream headers absent). Once fixed, OK to canary in us-east allowlist.
